symptoms.description: Skin appears red or flushed.
Irritating sensation causing a desire to scratch.
Peeling, flaking, or shed skin cells.
Fluid-filled bumps on the skin surface.
Skin feels rough, tight, or cracked.
Small pus-filled bumps on skin or near hair follicles.
Raised, thick patches of skin often covered with silvery scales.
Golden or yellowish dried crusts formed over oozing sores.
Painful, hot, or prickling sensation on affected skin.
Puffiness or fluid retention in skin tissues.
Loss of normal skin color resulting in white patches.
Open skin lesions causing localized pain.
Clogged skin pores filled with oil and dead skin cell debris.
Persistent central facial redness or visible tiny blood vessels.
Circular red patch with a clearer center and raised border.
Deep, firm, or fluid-filled lumps underneath the skin surface.
Sharp, localized neuralgic pain following a specific skin nerve pathway.
Raised, red or skin-colored welts that appear and fade rapidly.
Tiny, grey-white raised lines in skin folds or between fingers.
Darkened areas of skin caused by increased melanin production.
Redness extending across the bridge of the nose and cheeks.
Non-blanching red, purple, or brown spots caused by capillary bleeding.
Thick purulent fluid or pus discharging from an infected area.
Skin feels noticeably hot due to localized inflammation or infection.

diseases.name: Eczema
diseases.advice: Keep skin moisturized daily. Avoid harsh soaps and known triggers.
diseases.description: A chronic condition causing dry, red, itchy skin patches.

diseases.name: Allergic Contact Rash
diseases.advice: Identify and eliminate contact with foreign allergic substances. Apply cool compresses.
diseases.description: Skin reaction resulting from direct exposure to allergens or irritants.

diseases.name: Plaque Psoriasis
diseases.advice: Apply prescribed topical ointments, practice gentle skincare, and consult a dermatologist.
diseases.description: An autoimmune condition causing rapid skin cell buildup, leading to thick, scaly patches.

diseases.name: Hair Follicle Infection
diseases.advice: Clean the area gently with antibacterial soap and avoid tight clothing or shaving affected areas.
diseases.description: Inflammation or mild infection of one or more hair follicles.

diseases.name: Contagious Bacterial Skin Infection
diseases.advice: Consult a healthcare professional for topical or oral antibiotics. Avoid sharing towels.
diseases.description: A highly contagious bacterial skin infection common in young children and infants.

diseases.name: Acne
diseases.advice: Wash gently twice daily with mild cleanser. Use non-comedogenic skincare products.
diseases.description: Involvement of oil glands and hair follicles causing pimples and blocked pores.

diseases.name: Rosacea
diseases.advice: Avoid triggers such as hot drinks, spicy food, alcohol, and sun exposure.
diseases.description: A chronic inflammatory skin condition causing central facial redness and bumps.

diseases.name: Ringworm
diseases.advice: Apply topical antifungal cream twice daily. Keep skin dry and avoid sharing personal items.
diseases.description: A fungal infection causing a circular rash with clearer center skin.

diseases.name: Dandruff / Seborrheic Eczema
diseases.advice: Use medicated antifungal or anti-dandruff shampoos containing zinc pyrithione or ketoconazole.
diseases.description: An inflammatory skin condition affecting oily areas like scalp, face, and chest.

diseases.name: Shingles
diseases.advice: Seek immediate medical evaluation for antiviral therapy within 72 hours of outbreak.
diseases.description: Reactivation of the varicella-zoster virus causing a painful, blistering rash along nerve paths.

diseases.name: Hives
diseases.advice: Take oral antihistamines and avoid overheating or exposure to triggering substances.
diseases.description: Vascular skin reaction characterized by itchy, transient welts or wheals.

diseases.name: Scabies Infestation
diseases.advice: Consult a physician for prescription permethrin cream. Wash clothing and bedding in hot water.
diseases.description: Contagious skin infestation by microscopic mites causing severe nocturnal itching.

diseases.name: Bacterial Cellulitis
diseases.advice: Seek urgent medical evaluation for oral or intravenous antibiotic treatment.
diseases.description: A serious, deep bacterial skin and soft tissue infection requiring rapid medical care.

diseases.name: Vitiligo
diseases.advice: Protect depigmented skin with broad-spectrum sunscreen. Consult a dermatologist for phototherapy.
diseases.description: An autoimmune condition causing progressive loss of pigment patches on the skin.

diseases.name: Chloasma / Hyperpigmentation
diseases.advice: Apply high SPF sunscreen daily and minimize direct sun and heat exposure.
diseases.description: Skin condition causing dark, discolored symmetrical patches on sun-exposed facial areas.

diseases.name: Lupus Rash
diseases.advice: Consult a rheumatologist or dermatologist for systemic evaluation and light protection.
diseases.description: An autoimmune disorder causing a characteristic malar rash triggered by sun light.

diseases.name: Pityriasis Rosea
diseases.advice: Use mild emollients and anti-itch medications; rash usually resolves spontaneously in 6-8 weeks.
diseases.description: A benign, self-limiting skin rash starting with a single herald patch followed by oval lesions.

diseases.name: Acne Inversa
diseases.advice: Maintain warm compresses, avoid tight clothing, and consult a dermatologist for anti-inflammatory care.
diseases.description: A chronic inflammatory condition causing painful nodules and abscesses in body folds.

diseases.name: Pityriasis Versicolor
diseases.advice: Apply topical antifungal cleansers or lotions containing selenium sulfide.
diseases.description: A common superficial fungal infection leading to discolored, fine-scaling patches.

diseases.name: Solar Keratosis
diseases.advice: Schedule an examination with a dermatologist due to potential precancerous risk.
diseases.description: A rough, scaly patch on sun-damaged skin that may progress to squamous cell carcinoma.

diseases.name: Pompholyx
diseases.advice: Apply thick moisturizing ointments and cool compresses; avoid frequent hand washing.
diseases.description: A specific type of eczema causing intensely itchy, tiny blisters on palms, soles, and fingers.

diseases.name: Cutaneous Vasculitis
diseases.advice: Requires prompt clinical evaluation to determine underlying cause and organ involvement.
diseases.description: Inflammation of skin blood vessels resulting in spotty discoloration and purpuric lesions.

diseases.name: Skin Boils
diseases.advice: Apply warm compresses; do not squeeze or puncture. Seek professional drainage if painful.
diseases.description: A localized collection of pus within tissues caused by bacterial infection.

diseases.name: Molluscum
diseases.advice: Avoid scratching lesions to prevent spreading. Consult a doctor for options if persistent.
diseases.description: A viral skin infection causing small, firm, firm dome-shaped bumps with central dimples.

diseases.name: Erythema Nodosum
diseases.advice: Elevate legs and rest. Consult a healthcare provider to investigate underlying causes.
diseases.description: An inflammatory disorder producing tender, red nodules typically located on the shins.
